_purpose: Defines the runnable agent interaction implemented by task/adapter.py: what role the agent-under-test plays, what it is shown, what it must output, how conditions are assigned, and which materials/evidence back each design choice.
title: Generalized second-price auction bidding under bid-adjustment frictions
how_to_run:
python3 task/adapter.py --smoke-test    # offline sanity check, no network
python3 task/adapter.py --study human_main --cost 0.1 --alpha 0.5 --num-matches 10 --agent-policy truthful --seed 1
python3 task/adapter.py --study human_mechanism --cost 0.0 --info-cost 0.5 --num-matches 10 --agent-policy truthful --seed 1

participant_role.description: The agent-under-test plays the role of ONE of three anonymous group members ('participants' in the paper's own subject-facing language) across a sequence of matches. Each match, the agent is privately shown its own value for Good 1 (Good 2's value is alpha * Good 1's value), and must submit an initial bid and may revise it at successive decision points, subject to the session's bid-adjustment cost C.

environment_parameters.value_distribution: U{1,...,10} for Good 1's value, redrawn independently per match per participant (matches 1-4 style in human_main; the seed-matching used by the paper in matches 5-10 is NOT reproduced here -- see derived_design_decisions D2)
environment_parameters.payoff_formula: winner of slot k pays the (k+1)-th highest bid; payoff = alpha_k*(value - price) - bid_adjustment_costs_incurred_this_match [+/- information_costs_incurred_this_match for human_mechanism]

decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.period_index: int, 1-based decision checkpoint within the match
decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.is_first_decision_in_match: bool (true => placing the initial bid is free regardless of condition)
decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.alpha: float, value of Good 2 relative to Good 1
decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.current_own_bid: float or null if no bid placed yet
decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.info_cost: float or null; only present for study=human_mechanism
decision_point_state_shown_to_agent.counterfactual_payoff_table: object or null; only present for study=human_mechanism AND the agent chose to purchase it this period (see agent action 'view_info')

agent_action.bid: number in [0,10], required each period (repeating current_own_bid means no change / no cost)
agent_action.purchase_info: bool, only meaningful for study=human_mechanism; requests the counterfactual_payoff_table on the NEXT call, at cost info_cost for this period

match_end_record.winner_slot_by_participant: mapping of participant id -> 1, 2, or null
match_end_record.num_info_purchases_by_participant: mapping of participant id -> int (human_mechanism only)

run_output_metrics.mean_bid_adjustments_by_rank: as in paper Table 2 / Table 5 / Table 8
run_output_metrics.mean_bid_to_value_ratio_by_rank: as in paper Table 3 / Table 6 / Table 9
run_output_metrics.mean_allocative_efficiency: as in paper Figure 1 / Table 7 / Table 10

co_players.description: The other two group members each match are simulated policies, NOT replayed human data (the paper does not release individual human bid trajectories, and this package was built without external/OSF access -- see audit AUD-04). Available built-in policies are documented in task/adapter.py: 'truthful' (bid = value; the theoretical weakly-dominant benchmark the paper itself cites for the lowest-valued bidder, evidence_id ev.comp.env.setup) and 'softmax_explorer' (a stylized Boltzmann explorer parameterized like the paper's OWN Q-learning agents in Section 3.2.1, evidence_id ev.comp.qlearning.params, provided only as a stress-test opponent, not a claim about human behavior).
co_players.fidelity_caveat: Because co-players are simulated rather than real humans or a verified behavioral-clone of the paper's subjects, this task can score the agent-under-test's OWN exploration / bid-to-value / responsiveness-to-C behavior, but it cannot be used to reproduce the paper's between-subjects human-vs-human significance tests (Tables 5-10). evaluation.py reflects this: descriptive metrics run; inferential replication returns not_ready.

derived_design_decisions.decision: Discretize the continuous-time bidding window (human_main) into a bounded sequence of decision checkpoints instead of true continuous mouse-tracked time, since an LLM-style agent interacts turn-by-turn rather than via continuous mouse position.
derived_design_decisions.parameters_used: min 20 checkpoints, then 1%-per-checkpoint termination probability, capped at 100 checkpoints (mirrors T=100 used in the paper's OWN computational model, ev.comp.qlearning.params), matching the reported EXPECTED duration (2 minutes / ~120 one-second periods) but not the literal continuous silent-mouse protocol (ev.human_main.silent_protocol, ev.human_main.random_termination), which has no turn-based analogue.
derived_design_decisions.impact: Bid-adjustment COUNTS from this task are not directly comparable to Table 2/5 counts; ratios and directional effects of C and alpha are the intended comparison, not absolute adjustment counts.

derived_design_decisions.decision: Private values are drawn independently at random each match for every simulated run, rather than reproducing the paper's matches-5-10 common-random-seed matching across treatments (ev.human_main.value_generation) -- that scheme exists to let the PAPER compare human sessions apples-to-apples; a single adapter run has no cross-session comparison to protect.
derived_design_decisions.impact: Researchers who want the exact matched-value design for cross-run comparability must supply their own seeding scheme; adapter.py exposes --seed for run-level reproducibility only.

derived_design_decisions.decision: For study=human_mechanism, the discrete-period termination process (no stated minimum duration, probability 0.1 per period, expected 10 periods) is implemented directly per ev.human_mechanism.discrete_time_protocol, but the paper's own 4 duration-SEQUENCE realizations (Online Table N.1) are not available, so periods are drawn fresh via the RNG rather than replayed from the paper's fixed sequences.
derived_design_decisions.impact: Run-to-run period-count variance will not exactly match the paper's 4 canonical sequences.
